title: Rubik and Jabs reanalyse the Michelson-Morley ether data

tellings.quote: Beverly Rubik who's a biophysicist um and Harry Jabs who's a physicist they looked at that data and and and they wrote a paper basically saying well wait a minute there actually was an effect

plain: The Michelson-Morley experiment, a famous physics test that looked for an invisible 'ether' thought to carry light and is remembered for finding nothing, may in fact have found a small effect after all. That is what a biophysicist named Beverly Rubik and a physicist named Harry Jabs argued in a paper after going back over the original data, according to the psychiatrist and researcher Diane Powell, who summarises it without naming the paper. If they are right, a result taught as a clean 'no' would need a second look.
